chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Baḥr, from Kirdīn al-Mismaʿī, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام saying: “A man should not dye himself while he is in a state of janābah, nor should he perform ghusl while he is dyed.”

key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in the state of janābah requiring ghusl
key_terms.مُخْتَضِبٌ: being in a state of having applied dye
key_terms.يَخْتَضِبُ: applies dye, especially to the hair or beard

ai.seo_question: Can a person in the state of janābah apply dye or perform ghusl while dyed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the state of janābah and the use of dye. It indicates that one should not apply dye while junub, and should not perform ghusl while already in a dyed state.
